query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but its poor oxygen resistance limits practical high-temperature use. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing the alloy’s useful mechanical performance? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention and mechanism, the predicted change relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr, the relevant temperature, atmosphere, exposure time, and mechanical-loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a small fraction of aluminum (about 1–2 at.%) to cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will foster a protective Al2O3 surface scale at high temperatures, mitigating oxygen ingress without reducing the alloy’s strength or ductility.
generation.material_initial_state: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr with 8–16% RT ductility and 163–530 MPa 1000 °C yield strength, but poor oxygen resistance.
generation.intervention: Introduce 1–2 at.% Al into the HfNbTaTiZr composition during melting and casting.
generation.conditions: Exposure to air at 1000 °C for durations up to 100 hours, under uniaxial loading at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1.
generation.structural_mediator: Protective Al2O3 surface film forming on the alloy upon high-temperature exposure to air.
generation.mechanism: Aluminum in the alloy locally oxidizes to create a dense Al2O3 scale, acting as a barrier to oxygen diffusion and preventing embrittlement.
generation.predicted_outcome: Comparable yield strength (≥163 MPa) at 1000 °C with improved oxidation resistance and maintained ductility relative to unmodified cast HfNbTaTiZr.
generation.baseline: Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr exposed to high temperature in oxidizing environments suffers compromised ductility and strength from oxygen infiltration.
generation.boundary: Aluminum content above ~3 at.% may risk undesirable phase formation or decreased mechanical properties, requiring further verification.
generation.uncertainty: The exact aluminum concentration for optimal oxidation resistance and mechanical performance trade-off remains to be fully established.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two alloy batches (HfNbTaTiZr and HfNbTaTiZr + 2 at.% Al). Expose both sets to air at 1000 °C for 100 hours under constant tensile load at 10−3 s−1 strain rate, then measure their strength retention and oxygen profile.
measurements: Oxide layer thickness and composition (e.g., via SEM/EDS)
Oxygen concentration profile inside the alloy cross-section
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Al-bearing alloy does not exhibit a consistently thinner, denser oxide scale and superior mechanical performance (strength and ductility) relative to the baseline under identical conditions, the hypothesis is falsified.
